llms.txt & API Reference ​

Goryu can publish a machine-readable index of your HTTP API so that coding agents, LLM clients, and other tools can discover your endpoints without you writing docs by hand. One call — app.MountLLMs() — serves two documents built from your live router:

  • GET /llms.txt — an llms.txt Markdown document.
  • GET /llms.json — the same information as structured JSON.

Both are generated from the routes you actually registered, so they never drift from your code.

Features ​

  • Zero maintenance: the reference is derived from the router at request time.
  • Two formats: human/LLM-friendly Markdown (llms.txt) and machine-readable JSON (llms.json).
  • Named routes: route names, when set, appear as endpoint descriptions.
  • Programmatic access: build the same data in Go with app.APIReference() or render the Markdown with app.LLMsText().

Usage ​

Mount the endpoints ​

Call MountLLMs() after your routes are defined, so it captures the full set.

go
package main

import "github.com/arthurlch/goryu"

func main() {
    app := goryu.New(goryu.Config{AppName: "Acme API"})

    app.GET("/health", healthHandler)
    app.POST("/chat/stream", chatStream)
    app.GET("/chat/schema", chatSchema)

    app.MountLLMs() // registers GET /llms.txt and GET /llms.json

    _ = app.Listen(":3000")
}

AppName from your goryu.Config becomes the document title; if unset it defaults to API.

GET /llms.txt ​

Served as text/plain, following the llms.txt convention — a title, a > summary, and a list of endpoints:

bash
curl http://localhost:3000/llms.txt
text
# Acme API

> Acme API — HTTP API built with goryu, exposing 5 endpoints.

## Endpoints

- `GET /health`
- `POST /chat/stream` — ChatStream
- `GET /chat/schema` — ChatSchema
- `GET /llms.txt`
- `GET /llms.json`

The trailing — Name on each line is the route's name (from your route registration), used as a short description when present.

GET /llms.json ​

The same reference as JSON, matching the APIReference type:

bash
curl http://localhost:3000/llms.json
json
{
  "name": "Acme API",
  "summary": "Acme API — HTTP API built with goryu, exposing 5 endpoints.",
  "routes": [
    { "method": "GET",  "path": "/health" },
    { "method": "POST", "path": "/chat/stream", "name": "ChatStream" },
    { "method": "GET",  "path": "/chat/schema", "name": "ChatSchema" },
    { "method": "GET",  "path": "/llms.txt" },
    { "method": "GET",  "path": "/llms.json" }
  ]
}

Build the reference in Go ​

You don't have to serve the endpoints to use the data. APIReference() returns the structured reference, and LLMsText() returns the rendered Markdown.

go
ref := app.APIReference()
fmt.Println(ref.Name)          // "Acme API"
fmt.Println(len(ref.Routes))   // number of registered routes
for _, r := range ref.Routes {
    fmt.Printf("%s %s %s\n", r.Method, r.Path, r.Name)
}

markdown := app.LLMsText() // the exact body served at /llms.txt

This is useful for writing the reference to a file at build time, embedding it in a status page, or feeding it to another tool.

Types ​

APIReference and APIRoute are exported from the goryu package.

go
type APIRoute struct {
    Method string `json:"method"`
    Path   string `json:"path"`
    Name   string `json:"name,omitempty"`
}

type APIReference struct {
    Name    string     `json:"name"`
    Summary string     `json:"summary"`
    Routes  []APIRoute `json:"routes"`
}

Methods ​

MethodReturnsDescription
app.APIReference()APIReferenceStructured reference built from the router
app.LLMsText()stringThe llms.txt Markdown body
app.MountLLMs()—Serves GET /llms.txt and GET /llms.json

Why it helps agents and clients ​

llms.txt is a proposed convention (see llmstxt.org) for giving LLMs a concise, curated entry point to a site or service. For a Goryu API it turns your service into something an agent can reason about:

  • Discovery: a coding agent can GET /llms.txt to learn every route, method, and name — no OpenAPI file or scraping required.
  • Grounding: point an assistant at /llms.txt before it writes a client, and it will call the endpoints that actually exist rather than hallucinating them.
  • Tooling: /llms.json is trivial to parse, so IDEs, dashboards, or client generators can consume it directly.

Pair with request schemas and MCP

Serve a /schema route (via goryu.Schema[T], as the AI scaffolds do) alongside MountLLMs() so agents can discover both the endpoints and their request shapes. For an interactive workflow, run the goryu mcp server so agents can list routes and scaffold handlers directly.

Mount after routes, and mind exposure

MountLLMs() only reflects routes registered before it runs — call it last. Since it publishes your route map, gate it behind auth or restrict it to internal networks if your API surface is sensitive.
